## Purpose
Defines `KernelServices`, the concrete object `ExecutionEngine.execute()` attaches to a run as `ctx.runner` — the single seam through which capabilities (strategies, deliverable resolvers, context providers, gates, validators, hooks) reach the kernel and `app.*` runtime primitives without importing `agents.execution_engine` themselves (an import-linter contract forbids `agents.capabilities -> agents.execution_engine`). It does not reimplement engine behavior; it wraps and delegates to `engine.py`'s existing private methods (`_run_agent`, `_run_validation_fix_loop`, `_run_review_gate`, `_dual_write_artifact`, etc.) so routing execution through capabilities stays byte/event-identical to the legacy inline engine paths.

## Shape
- `KernelServices` — constructed once per run inside the engine's `_execute_impl`, holding the per-run invocation context (engine instance, ordered `AgentSpec`s, `RunSandbox`, run id, planning context, `ExecutionContext`); its public methods are the entire contract capabilities call off `ctx.runner`.
- `run_agent(step, ctx, ...)` — the run-one-agent primitive; rebuilds the engine's positional `_run_agent` call from the minimal `(step, ctx)` contract and re-yields its events unchanged.
- `run_validation_fix_loop(...)` / `FixPolicy` — the generic, config-driven Both-validation (`static_check` + `render_check`) bounded fix-loop, delegating to `engine._run_validation_fix_loop`; `FixPolicy` carries the deliverable name, max attempts, and failure mode instead of hardcoding `prototype.html`.
- `DeliverableContext` — the kernel-pure validation target (`path`/`content`/`runner`/`step`/`task_meta`) a registered `Validator` receives, built via `deliverable_context()`; carries `runner=self` so a validator reaches `static_check`/`render_check`/audit writers dynamically without importing the kernel.
- `run_fanout` / `run_worker` / `run_merge_agent` / `resolve_merge_strategy` / `agent_exists` — the Phase-11 fan-out spawn, per-worker invocation, isolated-workspace allocation/reclaim, and conflict-merge seams, delegating to `agents.execution_engine.fanout`.
- `run_human_gate` — routes a declared `gates:[human|approval]` step through the engine's unchanged `_run_review_gate`, the one HITL delegate.
- Audit writers (`record_gate_event`, `record_validation_result`, `record_hook_run`, `record_exec_run`, `record_subagent_run`, `record_wave_run`, ...) — best-effort, owner/workspace-scoped writes through the per-run `ScopedStore`; every one degrades to `None`/no-op on failure rather than aborting the run.
- `persist_task_html` / `write_fragment_artifact` / `write_merge_conflict_artifact` — typed-graph and durable-store artifact persistence so downstream steps/resumes can read a task's output back via `latest_typed_content`.

## Why this shape
The module's own docstring states the design intent directly: it factors the kernel-facing surface out of `engine.py` into one seam so capabilities can be swapped onto the strategy-driven architecture without re-implementing engine internals or violating the capabilities→execution_engine import boundary, while every delegated call stays semantically and byte-identical to the pre-existing engine behavior (INV-3 parity).
